Colour/state resolution through tokens/versions/v0_192/{_md-sys-color.scss,_md-sys-state.scss}.
provenance.edition-pin: v0.192, per the owner's standing decision. THE LARGEST STRUCTURAL edition delta this registry has found for slider specifically: `latest`'s token set is SPLIT into FIVE size variants (_md-comp-slider-{xsmall,small,medium,large,xlarge}.scss) replacing v0.192's single flat token set entirely — a real, sourced redesign (M3 sliders gained a `size` axis at some point after v0.192), FLAGGED LOUDLY rather than silently followed. Every value in this column is v0.192's single-size token set, per standing policy, not relitigated.
provenance.range-is-a-boolean-prop: slider.ts: `@property({type: Boolean}) range = false` forks `value` (single mode) into `valueStart`/`valueEnd` (range mode) on the SAME custom element — CONFIRMED by reading the class directly, the third distinct answer this matrix records to 'how does one component become a range slider' (Salt: two components; shadcn: array length; M3: this boolean).
provenance.handle-is-narrow-and-clipped: render()'s own `renderInput()` renders a FULL-TRACK-WIDTH `<input type="range">` per thumb (`width:100%; height:100%` in _slider.scss), then CLIPS each one to its own half of the track via `clip-path: inset(...)` computed from the midpoint between the two thumbs' current fractions (`.ranged input.start { clip-path: inset(0 $_clip-to-end 0 0) }` etc.) — a genuinely different mechanism from this chassis's own choice (narrow, per-thumb-centred inputs, matching Salt's own real mechanism instead — see the template's behavior.chassis note) to avoid needing the same clip-path midpoint math for a range pair.
provenance.primary/on-primary/on-surface/on-surface: md-sys-color.values-light()/values-dark(), v0.192 — the SAME hex pairs every prior M3 column in this pipeline resolves (#6750a4/#d0bcff primary, #fff/#381e72 on-primary, #1d1b20/#e6e0e9 on-surface, #49454f/#cac4d0 on-surface-variant, #e6e0e9/#36343b surface-container-highest, the SAME container colour card.m3.json/switch.m3.json both already resolved). Re-derived here for a self-contained column, not borrowed.
provenance.handle-colour-is-interaction-invariant: RE-VERIFIED BY READING THE TOKEN VALUES DIRECTLY, because the first pass assumed hover/focus/pressed would recolour the handle the way checkbox's/switch's own M3 columns did. They do NOT: `handle-color`, `hover-handle-color`, `focus-handle-color`, and `pressed-handle-color` are ALL literally `primary` — the SAME value, all four, confirmed by reading all four token lines side by side in _md-comp-slider.scss. This is a STARKER finding than switch's own M3 column (which at least varied handle colour between selected/unselected, even if hover/focus/pressed collapsed together within each) — slider's own handle NEVER changes colour, at ANY interaction state, EVER, in v0.192. All visible interaction feedback lives entirely in the ripple/state-layer (hover-state-layer-opacity 0.08, focus/pressed-state-layer-opacity 0.12, the SAME edition-dependent trio every prior M3 column has flagged) and, at focus/hover/active, the CSS-only value-label appearing.
provenance.no-host-cursor: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, grepped directly against the whole of _slider.scss: no `:host { cursor: ... }` rule anywhere — a real, sourced CONTRAST with switch's own M3 column (SWITCH-MATRIX.md finding 6), which DOES write one. The slider's own cursor comes entirely from the native `input[type=range] { cursor: pointer }` rule instead (see style.thumb.cursor).
provenance.min-width-floor: `:host { min-inline-size: 200px }` — a real, sourced minimum-width floor unique to this M3 column among the three; re-checked because neither Salt's nor shadcn's own root imposes one.
provenance.disabled-math: `:host([disabled]) { opacity: var(--_disabled-active-track-opacity) }` = 0.38 (component-wide). `.track::before` (inactive) gets a LOCAL compensating opacity, `calc((1 / var(--_disabled-active-track-opacity)) * var(--_disabled-inactive-track-opacity))` = calc((1/0.38)*0.12) ≈ 0.3158, so its FINAL visible opacity nets to the token's own intended 0.12 after the host-level multiplication — real, sourced CSS arithmetic, not an approximation. Colours: disabled-active-track-color/disabled-inactive-track-color/disabled-handle-color ALL resolve to on-surface.
provenance.no-readonly-no-format-family: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, grepped directly: no readonly-related @property anywhere in slider.ts; no format-callback mechanism of any kind — value display is either the raw number or a per-instance STATIC STRING override (valueLabel/valueLabelStart/valueLabelEnd), never a computed function.

structure.track.source: .track div; two-tone look drawn via ::before (inactive)/::after (active) in _slider.scss

structure.fill.source: .track::after — the SAME pseudo-element handles both single and range modes, range geometry done via clip-path

structure.thumb.value: a solid-filled circular disc (.handleNub) nested inside a larger 40px ripple/state-layer hit-area (.handle)

structure.value-readout.source: renderLabel(), a scale(0)->scale(1) pill, opt-IN via `labeled` (@property, default false)

structure.ticks.source: renderTrack(): ${this.ticks ? html`<div class="tickmarks">` : nothing}, opt-in via `ticks` (@property, default false)

behavior.role.value: implicit, free from the native <input type="range">
behavior.role.source: no explicit role written anywhere in slider.ts

behavior.value-announcement.value: implicit aria-valuenow from the native input, PLUS explicit PER-THUMB aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax (narrower than the overall min/max in range mode) and a getter-computed aria-valuetext

behavior.keyboard-value-change.value: genuinely NATIVE — no keydown override computes new values at all; handleKeydown exists only to track which input is being dragged for the range-overlap flip/clamp logic
behavior.keyboard-value-change.source: slider.ts handleKeydown -> startAction(), no value computation

behavior.pointer-drag.value: genuinely NATIVE — the real input spans the full interactive area and the browser performs the drag; M3's own pointer listeners exist only to track hover state for the ripple

behavior.track-click-jump.value: genuinely FREE — the native input's own hit area spans the full track width, so clicking anywhere on the track is clicking the input directly

behavior.value-readout-visibility.value: shown on hover, focus-within, or active — PURE CSS, no JS state at all

behavior.disabled-handling.value: native ?disabled on each input, PLUS a component-wide opacity dimming and per-part colour swap — see disabled-math

behavior.form-participation.value: a full form-associated custom element — single mode: String(this.value); range mode: a FormData with TWO entries (nameStart/nameEnd), the SAME two-named-values shape Salt's own RangeSlider uses, arrived at independently

prop.value-shape.value: ONE component, a range:boolean property forking value into valueStart/valueEnd

prop.step-multiplier.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no equivalent property; PageUp/PageDown use the browser's own native range-input large-step heuristic

prop.value-format.value: STATIC STRING overrides per instance (valueLabel/valueLabelStart/valueLabelEnd) — a genuinely different mechanism from Salt's own callback, falls back to the raw value when unset

prop.restrict-to-marks.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no equivalent concept; relies purely on step
